evidence: Cic. Inv. 1.48: crēdibile est quod sine ūllō teste audītōris opīniōne firmātur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Traupman also gives fidem habēre for “be credible”. Of things Cicero says so (vīsa, quae fidem nūllam habēbunt, Ac. 2.58, Lewis & Short s.v. fidēs); with a dative of the person the phrase means to trust someone.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 298.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
Lewis & Short: fides
